title: Khanna Calls Out Chinese Firms for Labor Abuses on US Soil
excerpt: The Silicon Valley congressman accuses Beijing-linked manufacturers of hiring undocumented workers and breaking US labor laws to undercut American industry.
body:
Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA) escalated his campaign against China's economic practices this week, publicly accusing Chinese companies operating inside the United States of hiring undocumented workers, violating labor laws, and competing on an illegally tilted playing field.

**What Khanna said:**
Appearing on Fox News, Khanna demanded the White House act — declaring that Chinese firms must not be 'opening manufacturing in the United States, subsidizing it and violating the law.' He also told viewers he was 'horrified' to spot Chinese steel unloaded at the Port of Cleveland, asking why American producers like Cleveland-Cliffs were being passed over.

**The bigger picture:**
Khanna, now the Ranking Member of the House Select Committee on Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, has been building a sustained case that China's labor suppression — including the use of forced labor — is 'particularly devastating for U.S. workers.' His Fox News appearance drew an immediate, expletive-laden response from President Trump on Truth Social, underscoring how politically charged the US-China manufacturing debate has become. Meanwhile, data Khanna has cited shows China's global trade surplus reached an unprecedented $1.2 trillion in 2025, even as US manufacturers shed tens of thousands of jobs.

**What to watch:**
With President Trump heading to Beijing, all eyes will be on whether Xi Jinping's government makes any concrete concessions on labor practices and state subsidies — the exact demands Khanna is pressing Trump to raise.
